name: Nonlinear Peelable Sign Set in a 319-Concept Expansion
definition: Let $S$ be the fixed 291-concept cornerless ample family with independent repairing tips $91$ and $157$, whose incident supports have binary encodings $102$ and $390$. Let $C$ be the union of the two punctured incident four-cubes and put $A=S\cup\{91,157\}$. The three components of $A\setminus C$ have orders $265,1,1$. Apply the one-coordinate component-label expansion to these components.
parameters: $|C|=26$, $|A|=293$, every expansion has $319$ concepts, and the twelve new-coordinate signed clauses split as ten clauses for the 265-vertex component and one clause for each tip.
properties: All eight component labelings are ample and exactly six are corner-peelable. The two nonpeelable labels are $(0,1,1)$ and its global reflection $(1,0,0)$. In particular, with the large component labeled zero, both $(0,1,0)$ and $(0,0,1)$ peel while their coordinatewise maximum $(0,1,1)$ does not. Thus the equality constraints that characterize ample expansion signings do not characterize the peelable subset. Each negative example has the proper nonpeelable section $S$ and is not a forbidden pc-minor. Exhaustive checks through $Q_3$ cover all 2244 nested nonempty ample pairs and 9656 new-clause assignments; exactly 5384 assignments satisfy the component equalities and shadow formula, and inverse component reflections recover every small fixed-shadow realization in every coordinate order.
